tickets.title: DataCore connection pool exhaustion under concurrent model inference requests
tickets.description: During the Apex Health POC trial (week of Mar 9), concurrent model inference requests from 3 parallel evaluation scripts exhausted the DataCore connection pool. New requests returned 503. The pool was hardcoded at 50 connections; peak demand hit 68. After pool exhaustion, the Auth0 token refresh cascade (INC-2026-001) hit an already-degraded system, compounding into the SEV1.
tickets.root_cause: DataCore connection pool ceiling (50) insufficient for concurrent enterprise trial workloads. No circuit breaker to shed load gracefully.
tickets.fix: Connection pool ceiling raised to 150 (Mar 21). Async connection acquisition with 800ms timeout added. Circuit breaker stub added — full implementation deferred to DR-006 Stage 3 (Jul 31).
tickets.notes: SLA breach: 12-day resolution vs 7-day L3 SLA. Delayed by Apex Health POC constraint (fix required coordinating with active trial). Apex Health signed as enterprise customer Jun 16 — fix was a trust signal.

tickets.title: Model inference timeout on context windows >128 tokens — p99 latency spikes to 6.8s
tickets.description: Thornbridge Capital reported that financial document summarization workflows (averaging 180-token context) were timing out at a 5s client timeout. p99 latency measured at 6.8s for >128-token contexts — 3x higher than 128-token baseline. Customers with short timeout settings (e.g., 3s) were seeing near-100% failure rates for large documents.
tickets.root_cause: vLLM attention mechanism using incorrect batching configuration for variable-length inputs — processing 128-to-256-token inputs as if they were 256-token uniform batches, causing unnecessary padding and compute waste.
tickets.fix: Dynamic batching enabled. Attention padding corrected for variable-length inputs. p99 for 180-token requests dropped from 6.8s to 380ms after fix.
tickets.notes: Linked to INC-2026-003 (SEV2, Mar 19) which was first detected at infrastructure level before Thornbridge reported. Fix timeline aligned with incident remediation window.

tickets.title: Airflow task retry storm causes scheduler database saturation on DAG backfill
tickets.description: Post-INC-2026-004 (Apr 3 SEV1): The Airflow scheduler retry storm during DAG backfill saturated the metadata database, causing the scheduler to stop accepting new task instances. 9 customer pipelines failed — Thornbridge Capital among them. Root cause was a retry policy on critical path tasks set to `retries=10, retry_delay=timedelta(seconds=5)` — a combination that created 10× task fan-out within 50 seconds on backfill, overwhelming the Postgres scheduler DB.
tickets.root_cause: Airflow retry policy misconfiguration on high-cardinality DAGs. No circuit breaker at scheduler DB layer. Postgres connection limit (200) hit during fan-out.
tickets.fix: Retry policy corrected: `retries=3, retry_delay=timedelta(minutes=5)`. Postgres max_connections raised to 400. Scheduler DB monitoring added to DataDog dashboard. Partial mitigation — full remediation deferred to Temporal migration (PULSE M4).
tickets.notes: Engineering-identified ticket — no customer reported directly because pipeline monitoring auto-alerted before customer SLAs breached. SLA credits would have applied to Thornbridge and 2 other enterprise customers had the failure extended beyond 4 hours. 3h 42m total outage. Reinforces PULSE M4 urgency.

tickets.title: v1 API rate limit headers not present in v2 — client SDKs failing silently on 429
tickets.description: Nuvera Insurance began v1→v2 migration in late March. Their rate-limit handling code reads `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers to implement client-side backoff. The v2 API returns 429 but does not include these headers — causing Nuvera's SDK to silently fail and retry immediately, causing a retry storm.
tickets.root_cause: v2 API spec did not carry forward v1 rate-limit headers. The v2 design assumed clients would use `Retry-After` header instead — but this was not documented in migration guide and the v1 SDK did not use it.
tickets.fix: v2 API updated to include `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and `Retry-After` headers. Migration guide updated with header mapping table. v2 SDK updated to use both headers with v1-compatible backoff logic.
tickets.notes: Pattern: 6 migration cases (L1/L2) in March-April cited rate limiting confusion. This L3 ticket resolved the root cause. After fix, migration-related rate limit tickets dropped to zero in May.

tickets.title: Auth0 SSO session refresh race condition — users forced to re-authenticate every 15 minutes
tickets.assignee: Marcus Chen (ATLAS TPM) / Auth0 Engineering liaison
tickets.description: Thornbridge Capital enterprise users on SSO (Okta provider) were being forced to re-authenticate every 15 minutes despite tokens having a 60-minute lifetime. Issue began after the Apr 14 Auth0 configuration change that was part of ATLAS M4 (audit logging). The token refresh call was racing with a logging middleware that was incorrectly marking tokens as expired before the refresh completed.
tickets.root_cause: Audit logging middleware added in ATLAS M4 inserted a 200–400ms delay before token refresh response was returned. Auth0 client-side library interpreted missing response within its 150ms window as a 401, triggering forced re-auth.
tickets.fix: Logging middleware moved to async fire-and-forget model — no longer blocks token refresh response path. Auth0 client timeout extended from 150ms to 500ms as secondary guard.
tickets.notes: ATLAS M4 (audit logging, Apr 14) introduced the regression. Fixed Apr 29. This is the only post-M4 regression ticket — the fix landed before ATLAS M5 started.

tickets.title: Python SDK v2 batch inference returns results in non-deterministic order
tickets.description: Kestrel Partners' evaluation team reported that Python SDK v2 `batch_infer()` returned results in non-deterministic order — results were not guaranteed to correspond to the input order. Their evaluation scripts were silently producing incorrect results because result index 0 was not guaranteed to correspond to input index 0 when using async batch processing.
tickets.root_cause: vLLM async batch processing returns results as they complete — not in submission order. The SDK wrapper did not re-sort results by submission ID before returning. The v1 SDK used synchronous calls and had no such issue.
tickets.fix: SDK `batch_infer()` now tags each request with a submission index and re-sorts results by index before returning. A `preserve_order=False` flag added for callers who prefer raw async order for performance.
tickets.notes: Critical catch during Kestrel's evaluation. If unresolved, Kestrel would have likely flagged the SDK as unfit for production use. Fix was prioritized due to Kestrel's role in HORIZON's Closed Won trajectory.

tickets.title: Temporal workflow state deserialization error after 1.3→1.4 upgrade
tickets.description: After upgrading Temporal server from 1.3 to 1.4 (required for PULSE M4 FlowEngine migration), pre-existing workflow state stored in the Temporal persistence layer failed to deserialize correctly. 7 in-flight workflows threw `ProtoDeserializationException` and transitioned to ERROR state. These were low-volume test pipelines, not customer-facing, but the error pattern would have caused data loss if it hit production pipelines during migration.
tickets.root_cause: Temporal 1.4 changed the protobuf serialization format for workflow history payloads without providing a migration path for 1.3 workflows still in-flight. Engineering did not catch this in pre-migration testing because all test workflows were terminated before the upgrade.
tickets.fix: Pre-migration workflow termination procedure added to the Temporal migration runbook. All in-flight workflows must be drained to COMPLETED or CANCELLED before the upgrade. Temporal 1.4 rollback performed; upgrade retried with drain procedure — zero deserialization errors.
tickets.notes: Engineering-identified in pre-migration test environment — never reached customer data. Runbook updated. This delay contributed to PULSE M5 (NovaAI pipelines) 9-day slip.

tickets.title: v1 API response envelope differs from v2 — breaking change not in migration guide
tickets.description: VantagePoint Analytics discovered that v1 API returns responses in `{ data: ..., meta: ... }` envelope while v2 returns `{ result: ..., pagination: ... }`. Their integration layer directly mapped v1 field names — all 23 API consumers in their system require updates. This was not documented in the migration guide as a breaking change. VantagePoint cited this as a reason for delayed migration timeline.
tickets.root_cause: v2 response envelope was designed by a different API team than v1 without a breaking-change review against existing clients. Migration guide focused on endpoint URL changes, not response schema changes.
tickets.fix_plan: Migration guide update with full response schema diff table (in review). v2 compatibility shim being evaluated — would accept v1-formatted responses but this is controversial (creates another compatibility surface). Decision expected by Jul 1. VantagePoint migration timeline extended to account for schema update work.
tickets.notes: This ticket is linked to VantagePoint's DR-010 renewal. Elena Markov cited SUPP-008 as a migration blocker in the Jun 12 renewal terms call. James Okonkwo committed to a documented fix path by Jul 1.

tickets.title: Missing audit log entries for high-frequency API requests (>50 req/s per tenant)
tickets.reporter: Meridian Financial (enterprise prospect — SOC 2 requirements review)
tickets.description: Meridian Financial's security team performed a pre-procurement audit of NovaAI's audit logging completeness. They discovered that at >50 requests/second per tenant, the audit log write path was dropping ~3-7% of log entries — the audit log write was synchronous and began dropping under load. For a SOC 2 Type II audit, 100% log completeness is required. This was flagged as a potential deal blocker.
tickets.root_cause: Audit log write path was synchronous in-request, using a Postgres write with a 200ms timeout. At >50 req/s, Postgres write queue backed up and the timeout was exceeded, causing silent drops. The audit log was designed for ATLAS's expected 15 req/s baseline — not for Meridian Financial's 80+ req/s peak.
tickets.fix: Audit log writes moved to async Kafka producer — fire and forget with guaranteed delivery semantics. Kafka consumer writes to Postgres asynchronously. End-to-end audit log delivery confirmation added via Kafka offset tracking. Zero drops observed in load test at 120 req/s.
tickets.notes: SLA breach: 14 days vs 7-day L3 P1 SLA. Resolution delayed by Kafka infrastructure review (security sign-off required for new Kafka topic). Meridian Financial satisfied with fix — SOC 2 concern resolved. One of the audit log completeness controls (CC7.2 evidence) was updated in Vanta after this fix.

tickets.title: HORIZON iOS app crashes on re-authentication after background suspend >30 minutes
tickets.description: Kestrel Partners alpha testers reported that the HORIZON iOS app crashes when re-authenticating after being suspended in the background for more than 30 minutes (iOS 17.4 and later). The app transitions from background to foreground, triggers the Auth0 silent re-authentication flow, and crashes with an EXC_BAD_ACCESS in the token cache layer.
tickets.root_cause: iOS 17.4 changed the app lifecycle timing for background suspend → foreground resume. The token cache was being written to at the same time as the re-auth flow was reading from it — a race condition exposed by the new lifecycle timing. Swift concurrent access to a non-thread-safe token cache.
tickets.fix: Token cache refactored to use Swift actors (thread-safe concurrent access). Background/foreground lifecycle hooks updated for iOS 17.4+ timing. Crash rate: 0 in 2 weeks of alpha testing post-fix.
tickets.notes: Alpha feedback catch — would have been a P1 at beta launch if unresolved. Priya Kaur prioritized this as the top beta-blocker fix.

tickets.title: v2 API webhook delivery: retry exhaustion silently discards events after 3 attempts
tickets.description: Corinthia Bank's integration team discovered that v2 webhook delivery silently discards events after 3 failed delivery attempts with no dead-letter queue and no alert to the customer. Their integration monitoring caught 4 missing events during load testing. For financial services use cases, silent event loss is a compliance concern (GDPR Article 5 data integrity) and a potential deal blocker.
tickets.root_cause: v2 webhook retry policy: 3 attempts at 30s, 5m, 15m intervals, then discard. v1 had a 7-attempt policy with 24-hour DLQ. The v2 design decision to reduce retries was made for infrastructure cost reasons — the DLQ removal was not deliberate but a gap in the migration.
tickets.fix_plan: DLQ (dead-letter queue) to be added to v2 webhook delivery by Jul 15. Customer dashboard entry for DLQ events to be added by Jul 31. 7-retry policy to be restored with exponential backoff. Fix timeline aligned with Corinthia Bank contracting (closing Jun 30).
tickets.notes: Corinthia Bank flagged this during due diligence — not yet a customer at time of ticket creation. James Okonkwo committed to fix timeline in AE-led contracting call Jun 26. Fix planned before Corinthia Bank's production onboarding (targeted late July).

tickets.title: Airflow DAG import failures on Python 3.12 — incompatible operator syntax
tickets.description: Brightpath Education onboarded in May and began authoring custom DAGs. Their engineering team uses Python 3.12. Several Airflow operators in NovaGrid's managed DAG library use `TaskFlow API` decorator syntax that is incompatible with Python 3.12's stricter annotation enforcement. 3 of their 8 custom DAGs failed to import.
tickets.root_cause: NovaGrid's managed Airflow operator library was developed and tested against Python 3.10. Python 3.12 enforces PEP 563 (deferred annotation evaluation) by default, which breaks several `@task` decorator patterns in the library.
tickets.fix: Managed operator library updated to be compatible with Python 3.10–3.12. `from __future__ import annotations` added where needed. Python version matrix added to DAG authoring documentation.
tickets.notes: Low-urgency P3 — Brightpath Education was not impacted on their production pipelines (only on new DAG development). Resolved within 10 days. Pattern: as NovaGrid onboards more customers, Python version compatibility in managed libraries will become a recurring issue. PULSE migration to Temporal eliminates this concern long-term.

tickets.title: NovaAI API p99 latency regression after Model Serving 65% allocation (DR-007)
tickets.description: After DR-007 (Jun 4) reallocated Model Serving to 65% SPARK / 35% ATLAS, the ATLAS-dedicated Model Serving capacity dropped from the equivalent of ~8 GPU slots to ~4.5 GPU slots. Under peak load (10-11am PDT, when US enterprise customers are most active), NovaAI API p99 latency climbed from 340ms baseline to 580ms — exceeding the 500ms SLA target. Observed Jun 10 in DataDog during INC-2026-013 investigation.
tickets.root_cause: DR-007 correctly reallocated GPU headroom but did not account for the ATLAS production traffic growth since March — traffic has grown 2.4× (2 enterprise customers now vs 0 in March, plus expanded trials). The ATLAS 35% allocation was sized for March traffic, not June traffic.
tickets.fix_plan: Leo Nakamura + Karl Bergstrom to review Model Serving allocation at Jul 15 checkpoint (first scheduled DR-007 review). Options: (a) dynamic time-of-day scheduling — ATLAS gets higher allocation during US business hours, SPARK gets higher allocation during off-peak; (b) GPU capacity add (blocked by CHG-004 hiring freeze — new GPU budget requires CFO co-sign). Option (a) being prototyped.
tickets.notes: Not yet customer-reported. DataDog SLO alert is the signal. If p99 stays above 500ms through Jun 30 (ATLAS GA announcement), this becomes a PR risk — the press release should not follow a breach of the stated SLA. Tracking closely.

tickets.title: HORIZON Android push notifications not delivered on Android 14 — silent failure
tickets.description: Solaris Logistics alpha testers on Android 14 devices reported that route optimization alerts (push notifications) are not being received. The FCM delivery API reports successful delivery, but notifications are not appearing on device. This is a silent failure — no error shown to user. Solaris's operations team relies on push notifications for time-sensitive route changes.
tickets.root_cause: Android 14 introduced new notification permission handling (POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission, required since Android 13 but enforcement tightened in 14). HORIZON's Android app was not requesting this permission explicitly at first launch — relying on implicit permission grant that Android 14 no longer provides.
tickets.fix_plan: POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission request added to onboarding flow. Play Store submission update required. Fix being prepared for beta build (Jul 15 target). Not blocking soft GA Jul 31 (limited to Kestrel and Solaris — workaround is notification settings toggle in app).
tickets.notes: P3 because workaround exists (manual notification enable) and soft GA (Jul 31) is limited release. Must be resolved before App Store GA Aug 31. Priya Kaur tracking.

tickets.title: v2 API pagination cursor expires after 60 seconds — incompatible with batch ETL workflows
tickets.description: Finex Capital's data engineering team (signed Jun 22) began integrating with v2 API for batch ETL workloads. Their ETL process pages through large result sets (100K+ records) using cursor-based pagination. The v2 API cursor expires after 60 seconds — far too short for batch ETL which may take 15-20 minutes to process a full page before requesting the next cursor.
tickets.root_cause: v2 API cursor TTL was set to 60 seconds as a default to reduce server-side state overhead. The v1 API had a 30-minute cursor TTL. No migration guidance noted the TTL reduction.
tickets.fix_plan: v2 API to support configurable cursor TTL via request parameter (`cursor_ttl_seconds`, max 3600). Default remains 60s for interactive use cases. Fix targeted for Jul 15 (aligns with Corinthia Bank webhook DLQ fix sprint). Migration guide to be updated with ETL-specific pagination guidance.
tickets.notes: Finex Capital is a new customer (closed Jun 22) — this is their first week of integration. James Okonkwo flagged this as a pattern: 3 of the last 5 v2 migration tickets relate to ETL/batch workload assumptions that differ from v1. A 'MERIDIAN v2 Migration: Enterprise ETL Patterns' guide should be written before next migration cohort (Aug 1).

tickets.title: IAM token refresh cache TTL unit mismatch causing p99 latency spike
tickets.description: Two days after the NEXUS IAM production cutover, token refresh p99 rose from 180ms to 3.4s during the Europe morning peak. Root cause was a cache TTL configured in seconds but deserialized as milliseconds, so every cache entry expired effectively immediately and each refresh hit Auth0 directly. Fixed and redeployed same day.
tickets.resolution: TTL deserializer corrected; unit-typed configuration introduced for all duration values in the IAM service.

tickets.title: NovaAI inference API 5xx under GA production load - capacity and circuit breaking
tickets.description: Sustained inference load at ~3x pre-GA baseline saturated model serving queues and surfaced as 5xx to customers. Rolling 7-day uptime fell to 96.8%, below the 97% internal floor. Immediate mitigation was emergency capacity plus a rate limit on new tenant onboarding (DR-011). The structural fix was the F6 circuit breaker.
tickets.resolution: F6 circuit breaker shipped Jul 31 - sheds load into queuing rather than errors. Uptime recovered to 98.9%. Onboarding rate limit lifted Aug 3.
tickets.notes: SLA breach flag is accurate but needs context: this ticket stayed open 25 days by choice. The fast fix (more capacity) was applied in 90 minutes; the ticket tracked the structural fix through to production.

tickets.title: FlowEngine cutover batch 14 backfill saturating DataCore query engine
tickets.description: Unthrottled backfill during a FlowEngine cutover batch drove DataCore query p99 to 2.6s against a 2000ms SLO. Off-peak window, no customer impact.
tickets.resolution: Backfill throttled to 200 rows/sec; rate limit made a required runbook parameter.

tickets.title: Mobile session refresh token lifetime mismatch logging out beta users
tickets.description: Mobile clients held 24-hour IAM refresh tokens while the backend assumed 7 days, silently logging out roughly 60 beta users as the first cohort crossed the 24-hour boundary three days after soft GA.
tickets.resolution: Refresh token lifetime aligned to 7 days. Token lifetime moved into the shared IAM integration contract so mobile and backend read a single value.

tickets.title: v1 API gateway latency for remaining mid-market batch integrations
tickets.description: v1 gateway capacity was scaled down in July in step with the migration curve, but the 8 remaining mid-market customers include two high-volume batch integrations. Their share of a much smaller pool now drives p99 to 1.4s during batch windows.
tickets.resolution: Gateway scaled back to the June footprint pending the final 8 migrations. Remains open until MERIDIAN M6 closes.
tickets.notes: Direct operational cost of the M6 miss - v1 infrastructure has to stay warm for 8 customers.

tickets.title: Quarterly access review evidence export missing pre-IAM grant history
tickets.description: Following the auditor's evidence finding on CC6.4 and CC6.6, the IAM evidence exporter could only produce grant history from Jul 1 onward. Auditor remediation required compensating documentation covering the prior Auth0 workaround period, which had to be reconstructed from Auth0 logs and manual approval records.
tickets.resolution: Compensating documentation assembled and accepted by the auditor Aug 7. Exporter extended to ingest historical Auth0 grant records so the gap cannot recur during the observation period.

pattern_1_novaai_model_serving.summary: 5 tickets related to NovaAI model serving reliability and performance. Root causes cluster around: (a) connection pool sizing for concurrent enterprise load (SUPP-001, resolved via DR-006), (b) vLLM configuration for variable-context inference (SUPP-002), (c) SDK correctness for batch patterns (SUPP-006), (d) audit log write path blocking (SUPP-009), (e) GPU capacity allocation under traffic growth (SUPP-013, open). SUPP-013 is the current open risk — p99 SLA breach risk ahead of Jun 30 GA.
pattern_1_novaai_model_serving.tpm_recommendation: ATLAS TPM: SUPP-013 (GPU allocation / p99 latency) must be resolved or mitigated before Jun 30 GA announcement. Monitor DataDog SLO hourly. If p99 exceeds 500ms on Jun 29, consider time-of-day GPU scheduling (option a) as same-day mitigation.

pattern_2_pipeline_reliability.summary: 3 tickets related to Airflow and Temporal pipeline reliability. Pattern: Airflow retry storm (SUPP-003) and Temporal migration edge case (SUPP-007) both point to the fragility of the dual-run period. SUPP-012 (Python 3.12 compatibility) is a lower-severity operational issue. All 3 resolved. PULSE M4 FlowEngine (Jul 25) eliminates most of this surface area — but the Temporal migration runbook (SUPP-007 fix) must be treated as a live artifact.
pattern_2_pipeline_reliability.tpm_recommendation: PULSE TPM: The runbook updates from SUPP-007 must be reviewed before each migration cohort cutover. The pattern shows that migration testing environment must mirror production Python version and Temporal upgrade state precisely.

pattern_3_v2_api_migration_gaps.summary: 4 tickets exposing gaps between v1 and v2 API behavior that were not documented in the migration guide: rate limit headers (SUPP-004, resolved), response envelope schema (SUPP-008, in progress), webhook DLQ removal (SUPP-011, in progress), pagination cursor TTL (SUPP-015, open). Pattern: the v2 API was designed for interactive use cases — batch/ETL and compliance-heavy enterprise use cases are consistently hitting undocumented breaking changes. Two of these tickets (SUPP-008, SUPP-011) are directly linked to at-risk deals (VantagePoint and Corinthia Bank).
pattern_3_v2_api_migration_gaps.tpm_recommendation: MERIDIAN TPM: Prioritize 'Migration Guide v2: Enterprise Breaking Changes' documentation update before Aug 1 cohort. SUPP-008, SUPP-011, SUPP-015 fixes should be bundled into a single v2.1.0 compatibility release (target: Jul 15). Corinthia Bank and VantagePoint are watching this.

pattern_4_auth_session.summary: 2 tickets related to Auth0 session management edge cases. SUPP-005 (ATLAS SSO token refresh race condition, resolved) and SUPP-010 (HORIZON iOS crash on background resume, resolved). Both resolved. The common thread: Auth0 integration code in both ATLAS and HORIZON has subtle timing dependencies that are exposed by platform changes (iOS 17.4 lifecycle, ATLAS M4 logging middleware). NEXUS IAM deployment tonight (Jun 30) may introduce new auth edge cases — monitor closely.
pattern_4_auth_session.tpm_recommendation: All TPMs: NEXUS IAM deploying tonight. Auth0 session edge cases are a known risk area. Brief Kestrel and Solaris beta users to report any unexpected re-authentication prompts immediately. Sara Lindqvist to confirm Auth0 session TTL behavior is unchanged in IAM go/no-go at 9pm.

pattern_5_audit_compliance.summary: 1 L3 ticket (SUPP-009, audit log completeness under high request rate) with direct SOC 2 implications. Resolved Jun 3 — Kafka async write path fixed. The Meridian Financial discovery was a near-miss: if they had not caught this during pre-procurement review, it would have emerged during the auditor observation period (Sep–Nov 2026). SUPP-009 resolution was incorporated into Vanta control evidence for CC7.2.
pattern_5_audit_compliance.tpm_recommendation: SHIELD/ATLAS TPMs: Audit log completeness testing at realistic enterprise request rates (80+ req/s) should be added to the pre-the auditor evidence checklist. The fix is in production — but it should be validated in the Vanta automated check.
